articles.title: Supercell’s mo.co heads back into beta as studio plans major changes
articles.summary: Supercell has moved Mo.co back into beta development after admitting the monster-hunting game is not performing as well as hoped. The current version will remain in low maintenance while the team experiments with new ideas and works on what comes next.... [ MORE ]
body: Despite the company admitting last month that the title will need bigger changes to achieve mass appeal, Supercell said it believes in the game and has more ideas planned for future testing.
“We previously shared that mo.co isn’t performing as well as we had hoped, and it will need bigger changes to get where we want it to be," the company wrote in a post.
“With that in mind we’ve decided to move the game back to Beta. The current game will continue on low maintenance while we focus on experimenting, testing new ideas, and building what comes next."
The current game will not receive new weapons in upcoming seasons, while seasonal passes will lose their premium tracks and weapons.
points: Supercell has moved Mo.co back into beta development after admitting the monster-hunting game is not performing as well as hoped.

articles.title: Supercell’s monster hunting game Mo.co is going ‘back into beta’
articles.summary: Supercell’s Mo.co is heading ‘back into beta’ while its dev team rethinks how to proceed with the underperforming monster hunting game. “Mo.co is not performing as well as we hoped…it will need big changes to achieve mass appeal,” said Supercell on its Mo.co blog.
body: This means Mo.co will run “on low maintenance,” says Supercell, and no further weapons or premium tracks will be released. Elite merch and content “will be recycled from previous seasons.”

“Our goal is to release updates more frequently and reduce the wait between them,” the team explained, adding there was no date planned for the next update, but it expected to roll one out before the end of 2026.
“As the saying goes, sometimes you need to take one step back before taking two steps forward,” the team added.

The game’s community manager, Joao, revealed on X that as a result of the change, they will be redeployed to a different role within the company as the game no longer requires a full-time community manager.

articles.title: September’s Collabs Corner: Naruto in Free Fire, KPop Demon Hunters in Monopoly Go, Duo goes to battle in Brawl Stars, and more
articles.summary: Among the updates, announcements and marketing drives for mobile games, this bustling industry sees a never-ending flow of crossovers and collaborations. Some partnerships see characters from one game IP enter another. Others see brands or logos show up in unexpected places.
body: With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of all the latest collaborations happening on mobile.
Supercell’s Brawl Stars and learning app Duolingo have been building up to a collab for weeks with mascots Spike and Duo trading blows in online comments sections. Now, the partnership is official.

Duo is wreaking havoc in Brawl Stars with a 20v1 boss battle set inside a classroom - where players must take down increasingly powerful versions of Duo and answer quiz questions correctly, or else be eliminated.

Meanwhile, Spike has invaded Duolingo and is making himself at home, appearing inside lessons as part of a limited-time quest. Learners who finish the challenge this month can then unlock Spike in Brawl Stars too.

articles.summary: To help get you primed and ready for another week in mobile gaming, we’ve curated the biggest stories you need to know from the last seven days. 1) Brawl Stars and Duolingo launch global mascot crossover... [ MORE ]
body: Duolingo has teamed up with Supercell’s Brawl Stars to bring each game’s mascot to the other’s world.
Duo and Spike are currently mid-crossover after trading jabs in comments outside of the apps. The collaboration also includes events and rewards, including a boss battle in Duo’s classroom.
King staff in Sweden could go on strike after trade unions failed to reach an agreement with the Candy Crush maker.

A strike notice was issued on September 15th, with the strike itself going ahead on September 25th if an agreement cannot be reached. Members of the union are seeking greater security and influence over workplace conditions.
